author: masnax
body:
Takes the schema and entities from https://github.com/FuturFusion/operations-center/pull/9 and generates code using `incus-generate`. 

So unlike `sqlc`, you write your own struct definitions, and you can add fields that you want to ignore from generation with the `db:omit` tag. 

Then you just gun `go generate ./... ; gofmt -s -w . ; go imports -w`

Few big caveats with `incus-generate`:
* `incus-generate` does not support the `RETURNING` directive. Instead it returns the created ID so the row can be fetched again. We can add `RETURNING` support if that's needed, shouldn't be too hard.
* All tables need to have an `ID` column. The `storage_volumes` example used for `sqlc-poc` did not, so I had to add it here.
* It expects everything to be in a transaction, the helpers all expect a `sql.Tx`
* It expects you to have `stmt.go` boilerplate for registering prepared statements
* It heavliy depends on the `query` package from `incus`. In fact it pulls that import early on and hard-codes it into the generated files. Since they're in an `internal` package in incus right now, I copied over some relevant parts of the `query` package. You have to manually edit the generated imports in the generated files because of the hard-coding. For finding imports, `incus-generate` relies on `goimports` to be called afterward, so we can remove the hard-code from Incus to avoid this trouble.

As far as the type marshalling goes, `incus-generate` seems to be a bit cleaner with the `db:"marshal=yes"` tag as you only need to write `MarshalDB` and `UnmarshalDB` for each type and the `query` package handles the rest.

Some nice-to-haves with `incus-generate`:
* Filtering is pretty seamless as long as you don't need to nest any more than one level. You just get `(col1 and col2) or (col1 and col3) or ...`
* Sane API responses are built-in with Incus' `api.StatusError`, so failing to find an entity wraps a `404 not found`, inserting an entity that already exists wraps a `409 conflict`
* You get a [`<entity>Columns`](https://github.com/FuturFusion/operations-center/blob/6cf8b74616dc203ec521f91d381c5120ecddd18b/cmd/incus-generate/entities/clusters.mapper.go#L106-L108) helper to help with naming and ordering of columns
* You can create your own custom prepared statements and run them through [`get<Entites>`](https://github.com/FuturFusion/operations-center/blob/6cf8b74616dc203ec521f91d381c5120ecddd18b/cmd/incus-generate/entities/clusters.mapper.go#L111) if the generated SQL isn't good enough, or do one-off queries with [`get<Entities>Raw`](https://github.com/FuturFusion/operations-center/blob/6cf8b74616dc203ec521f91d381c5120ecddd18b/cmd/incus-generate/entities/clusters.mapper.go#L141)

author: jsquire
body:
* [Event Hubs] Fixed producer semaphore release

The focus of these changes is to fox an obscure edge case in the `EventHubBufferedProducer` client where an obscure race condition when flushing/enqueuing events concurrently with disposing the producer could cause a semaphore to be released inappropriately.  This error superseded the `TaskCanceledException` that should have been surfaced.

Also moved to volatile reads for the total buffer count when making state-related decisions, to ensure that the most recent value is used.

author: tilzen
body:
This PR introduces several improvements to the `dlauncher` configuration and user experience, including a user-friendly command to initialize the configuration, and clear error handling.

**Key Changes:**

1.  **Default Configuration File Generation (`init` command):**
    *   Introduces a new `init` command (e.g., `dlauncher init`) that creates a default `config.yaml` file at `~/.config/dlauncher/config.yaml` (or the path specified by the `DLAUNCHER_CONFIG_PATH` environment variable).
    *   This default configuration includes pre-configured shortcuts for `any`, `blank`, and `google` searches, as well as executable definitions for `chrome` and `firefox`.  This makes it easier for new users to get started.
    *   The `init` command also displays a message indicating the location of the newly created configuration file.  Example:
        ```
        dlauncher init
        Default configuration file created successfully at /home/user/.config/dlauncher/config.yaml
        ```

2.  **Improved Error Handling:**
    *   The `ParseConfig()` function now returns an error instead of panicking if the configuration file is not found. This provides a more user-friendly error message, guiding the user to create the configuration file using the `init` command. Example:
        ```
        dlauncher run -e chrome -s google
        config file not found at /home/user/.config/dlauncher/config.yaml.  Run 'dlauncher init' to create a default config file.
        ```

In summary, I didn't read the README, and then this happened :sweat_smile:

author: troykomodo
body:
Moves the clippy powerset stuff into the clippy job (only runs on a brawl run) and then adds a new job that runs `cargo package`. Cargo Package is a tool ran before `cargo publish` (it runs automatically unless you do `--no-verify`). This is a sanity check to test if the crate compiles before uploading it to crates.io. The reason we do this in a power-set is because we want to make sure that all features of the crate compile successfully. This is a known issue on crates.io where sometimes crates break and or dont work depending on the features they are enabled with.

CLOUD-63

This PR also splits our ci into components, to reuse existing setup code related to `setup-rust` where we install the rust tool chain, use a cache and install custom rust tools. As well as `setup-ffmpeg` where we install and configure ffmpeg.

CLOUD-64

## Why are the changes needed? - Today there is no endpoint to query worklfow execution metrics - Especially these metrics are interesting for users to reason about task runtimes ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/75cbc05f-2db5-4631-b204-e1c3b2505d6c) ## What changes were proposed in this pull request? - adding `get_execution_metrics()` endpoint for friendly client - adding model for `Spans` ## How was this patch tested? - running this on a couple of workflows with different shape: ``` python from flytekit.remote import FlyteRemote from flytekit.configuration import Config r = FlyteRemote(config=Config.for_endpoint(endpoint="demo.hosted.unionai.cloud")) # execution_id = "altzn6pfw8ll6n4h8tdq" # static # execution_id = "a964rbl6l9q4thkwzgnj" # static fail execution_id = "a2hpw4nh9vjhxsbst8nc" # static loop # execution_id = "atkjvqqhdkxpbzphqm7t" # dynamic loop # execution_id = "agmqkz8jp5cprw62c9kc" # dynamic starting # execution_id = "a5lk5bcqvjxnkpxvp5h2" # dynamic nested # execution_id = "amlm77lsv4mmm2gqmgm2" # Spark # execution_id = "abkhbrztrmqdx4jvzxh5" # static retries # execution_id = "afhtl6l89wsvx4r2glvt" # map over task fails currently, lets fix in a follow up PR project = "jan-playground" domain = "development" exec = r.fetch_execution(project=project, domain=domain, name=execution_id) a = r.client.get_execution_metrics(id=exec.id, depth=10) def handle_node(node): node_id = node.node_id.node_id if node_id != "": # Check for existing nodes in the execution for node_span in node.spans: task_id = node_span.task_id.task_id.name if node_span.node_id.node_id != "": handle_node(node=node_span) elif task_id != "": print(f"{node_id} - {task_id}") task_metrics = {} for operation_span in node_span.spans: task_metrics[operation_span.operation_id] = ( operation_span.end_time.seconds - operation_span.start_time.seconds ) print(task_metrics) for span in a.spans: handle_node(node=span) ``` Example output: ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/736639c7-4793-414e-9b86-4c434b510080) ## Check all the applicable boxes - [x] I updated the documentation accordingly. - [x] All new and existing tests passed. - [x] All commits are signed-off.

Summary by Bito

The implementation initially added a get_execution_metrics endpoint and Span model for workflow execution metrics, but was later refactored to remove the deprecated metrics module and Span model. The changes simplified the metrics retrieval logic through the friendly client while maintaining core capabilities for analyzing task runtimes and execution performance.

This creates a new trait, TlbFlushLockAccess, that is used to allow memory protections management code to access the VP's TLB flush and lock machinery. It then adds a new parameter of this type to certain methods on ProtectIsolatedMemory, and adds calls to it where appropriate.

This also adds a small hack to avoid an ongoing layering discussion. We're unsure of the right approach to fix it, but the rest of the code should be fine as-is.

body:
#### Problem

There are a couple of GitHub actions that use `ubuntu-20.04`, but this version will no longer be supported in April 2025. They also use versions of Python that are not found on later versions of Ubuntu. The `pylint` GitHub action also no longer works with a newer version of Python > 3.10: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/78459119

---

This PR updates the actions to use `ubuntu-latest` and updates the version of Python used in the `python format` and `pylint` actions to `3.9` to ensure compatibility with the latest Ubuntu version.

Fixes #582

author: picoliu
body:
Previously the `TestInterrupt()` test has a probability to fail, that is because
1. The interruption takes place before the generation task begins.
2. The interruption happens after the generation is over.

This PR fixes this problem by calling the `Interrupt()` function in the streaming callback to ensure generation is in process when `Interrupt()` is called.

author: calclavia
body:
This pull request introduces the following updates:

- **Dockerfile**: Introduces a Dockerfile to package the MCP for deployment across various environments.
- **Smithery Configuration**: Adds a Smithery YAML file, which specifies how to start the MCP and the configuration options it supports. It allows you to [deploy](https://smithery.ai/docs/deployments) your MCP to [Smithery](https://smithery.ai?utm_campaign=pr), serving it over WebSockets so end-users do not need to install additional dependencies. To deploy, merge this PR, then visit your [server page](https://smithery.ai/server/@donghao1393/mcp-dbutils?utm_campaign=pr&modal=claim) and click "Deploy" under the deployments page.
- **README**: Updates the README to include installation instructions via Smithery and a popularity badge. _Note that the installation only works after the server is deployed on Smithery._

Please review these updates to verify their accuracy for your server and feel free to customize it to your needs. Let me know if you have any questions. 🙂
